artworks.title: The Latona Fountain, Versailles
artworks.description: A monumental fountain in the gardens of Versailles, with sculpture by the brothers Gaspard and Balthazar Marsy. It depicts Latona, the Roman name of Leto, with her children Apollo and Diana, appealing to Jupiter as the Lycian peasants who insulted her are transformed into frogs, an episode told in Ovid's Metamorphoses. The subject is often read as a political allegory for Louis XIV, the triumph of royal order over insolence and revolt.

artworks.title: Latona and the Lycian Peasants
artworks.description: An oil by Annibale Carracci in the Archbishop's Palace at Kroměříž. Latona — Leto — cradles the infant twins as Lycian peasants muddy the spring she asked to drink from; frogs already gather at the water's edge. Ovid's episode of maternal wrath painted with Bolognese clarity, the Titaness as both suppliant and avenger.

artworks.title: Latona and the Lycian Peasants
artworks.description: A cabinet landscape in the Brueghel manner: Latona with Apollo and Diana at a woodland spring while the Lycian peasants who denied her water begin their metamorphosis into frogs. Tiny myth inside a dense Flemish forest — Leto's insult and revenge folded into the pleasure of looking at leaves and water.

artworks.title: Latona with Her Children Apollo and Diana
artworks.description: A sculptural group in the Los Angeles County Museum of Art showing Latona seated with the infant Apollo and Diana. The composition echoes the Versailles fountain type — the Titaness as protective mother of the twin archers — translating Leto's wandering maternity into a compact, collectible marble for the Enlightenment eye.

popCulture.title: Latona Fountain
popCulture.creator: Gaspard and Balthazard Marsy
popCulture.description: Versailles' Latona Fountain freezes Leto's Lycian vengeance in marble and lead — the mother of Apollo and Artemis as Louis XIV's allegory of divine right.

popCulture.title: Delos
popCulture.description: Leto's wandering ended on Delos — the island that received the birth of Apollo and Artemis, and still anchors her cult.

popCulture.title: Leto
popCulture.description: The Titaness mother of the twin archers remains the type of persecuted maternity — Hera's jealousy, and a birth that made an island holy.
